Govt approves extension of PM-KISAN scheme to all farmer; clears pension for farmers, traders

By:All India Radio - 1 June,2019

Short Detail

The newly-sworn in NDA government has approved the extension of Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) to all the farmers in the country. Earlier the benefit of the scheme was applicable to farmers having two hectares of land.

Nearly 14 crore 50 lakh farmers will be now covered under the revised scheme. The Minister said, total burden on the exchequer will be over 87,000 crore rupees for the year 2019-20.

Six thousand rupees per year is being given in three instalments to the farmers, under the scheme.

NOTE:Farmers over 60 will also be eligible for getting an additional Rs.3000 per month.

Modi govt decides to give shopkeepers, retail traders Rs 3,000 as pension

By:Business Standard - 31 May,2019

Short Detail

The Modi government in its first Cabinet meeting after assuming office for the second term had approved a new scheme, which assures minimum monthly pension of Rs 3,000 to all shopkeepers, retail traders and self employed persons after attaining the age of 60 years, fulfilling its poll promise.

An official also said that,"All shopkeepers and self employed persons as well as retail traders with GST turnover below Rs 1.5 crore and aged between 18-40 years can enrol for the scheme".

FDI inflows record first decline in six years in FY19

By:domain-B - 29 May,2019

Short Detail

Foreign direct investment (FDI) in India declined by 1 per cent to $44.37 billion in the 2018-19 financial year, registering the first fall in the last six years, as the wave of foreign fund flows into the telecom, pharma and other sectors subsided, official figures showed.

Last time FDI registered a contraction was in 2012-13 when foreign fund inflows declined of 36 per cent to $22.42 billion from $35.12 billion in 2011-12.

Indian Army Introduces New Restrictions on Buying Cheaper Cars From CSD

By:Times Now - 28 May,2019

Short Detail

The Indian Army has imposed restrictions on its officers and jawans with respect to purchasing cheaper cars from the CSD(Canteen Stores Department) Canteen.

A csd canteen. Source:The Economic Times

As per these restriction, Indian Army officers can now only buy a vehicle valued up to ₹12 lakh from the CSD Canteen and that too only once in eight years.

Indian Army jawans, on the other hand, can buy a car up to ₹6.5 lakh once during their service and once after their retirement from the CSD canteen.

Russia launches new icebreaker as country focuses on economic potential of the Arctic

By:Ottawa Citizen - 28 May,2019

Short Detail

Russia rolled out a new nuclear-powered icebreaker named Ural as it signals its further efforts to take advantage of the Arctic’s economic potential.

Russia's icebreaker Ural. Source:ottawacitizen.com

The Russian news agency TASS reported that besides breaking ice for convoys in the Arctic, the ships will help ensure transportation of hydrocarbons from the Yamal and Gydan peninsulas to the Asia Pacific market. The 173-metre long vessel has a new and improved reactor and a new turbine system so it can operate over its 40-year-lifespan.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that by 2035 Russia expects to operate 13 heavy icebreakers. Nine of those would be nuclear-powered.

India witnesses a decline in mobile internet speeds, rank falls to 121: Ookla

By:The Mobile Indian - 27 May,2019

Short Detail

India is witnessing a dip in mobile internet speeds, as per the latest data by Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index. This has brought down the country’s ranking to 121 from 120 in the previous month.

India witnesses a decline in mobile internet speeds, rank falls to 121. Source:whatphone.com.au

In December 2018, India ranked at 108 and it fell to 119 in January 2019 and then it remained steady with 120 position for the month of February and March 2019.

As per Ookla, India has a dip in mobile speeds with average download speed clocked at 10.71 Mbps. The upload for India was clocked at 4.20 Mbps. The report shows that Norway is currently leading the pack with an average download speed of 65.41 Mbps followed by Canada and South Korea with average download speeds of 64.42 Mbps and 63.81 Mbps respectively.

Mean while in the braodbad speed sticks at 68th position at 29.5Mbps in Downlaod and 24.84Mbps in Updload speed.
